newsitem.title: UK: UK minister sees Labour wishful thinking on prices.
newsitem.headline: UK minister sees Labour wishful thinking on prices.

text.p: Chief Secretary to the Treasury William Waldegrave on Tuesday accused Labour of "wishful thinking" on keeping price rises down and said their policies would make Britain a high inflation economy again.

Waldegrave was speaking to an audience in the City of London on the eve of a keynote speech by Labour economics spokesman Gordon Brown, in which he is expected to announce a Labour government would set a tough anti-inflation target.
"You may have heard rumours that Gordon Brown intends to copy our inflation target. But wishful thinking alone won't keep inflation low," Waldegrave said.
The government has said it aims to have inflation below 2.5 percent by the end of the current parliament. Brown has already said he will not set a looser inflation target than the government's.

Waldegrave said Labour would turn its back on Conservative structural reforms, which have been praised by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development as having contributed "to a more flexible and less inflation prone economy".
"Labour describe privatisation as the agenda of the past and they promise to sign up to the (European Union) Social Chapter and introduce a minimum wage," he said.
"Labour's policies would undermine this country's economic success and make Britain, once again, a high inflation economy."
Brown is due to make Wednesday's speech on inflation and the framework for setting monetary policy under a Labour government at 1800 GMT.
